statusDetail: All three defects are fixed, committed and open as PR #60. Defects 1 and 2 are PROVEN BY LIVE READS on the non-production app g162-v1-uat, with the violation measured before the fix and gone after it. Defect 3's refusal is proven at the route level (a named 500 with no SQL run) and is NOT proven on the deployed surface, because no deployed request can present a missing tenant binding: the app refuses such a request earlier, at 401, before any finance handler runs (measured, both legs). The lane did not stage a violation it could not produce. That single un-surface-proven clause is why this close is partial rather than full.

LESSON: A DigitalOcean app cannot reuse another app's EV[...] encrypted env value: 'secret env value cannot be decrypted'. Environment values must be written per app. The safe shape is a script that reads the plaintext from GCP Secret Manager, writes the spec file, and prints only key names — the value never touches a command line, a transcript or the repo.

A smartcity-os container exits non-zero at boot with a partial environment, and DO discards the runtime logs quickly (the deployment reaches final_cleanup and `doctl apps logs --type run` then answers 'no deployment found'). Read walrus-app's spec for its env KEY SET before building any UAT app for this repo, and add placeholder values for the keys you cannot source; the app's own environment is the right place to record which are placeholders.

On this fleet's Windows box, Node cannot reach a DO app without BOTH `--dns-result-order=ipv4first` (the host resolves AAAA-first and fetch dies with a bare 'fetch failed') and `--use-system-ca` (a fleet CA terminates TLS; without it, 'unable to verify the first certificate'). A healthy app looks completely dead to a probe run without them.

The loopback-only internal-context path (`x-internal-ai: smartcity-ctx` + `x-tenant-id`) is NOT spoofable from the internet on DO App Platform, even with a forged X-Forwarded-For: both routes.ts's /api gate and middleware/tenant.ts read req.ip and answered 401 in every attempt. Reaching a tenant-specific session route from outside therefore requires a real login.

requireTenant binds an anonymous caller to the demo tenant (slug 'your-city', id 1) — which holds ZERO mygov_fees rows. Any 'tenant 1' reasoning about this store must start from that read: tenant 1 is the empty demo city, tenant 2 is Bastrop, and all 311,736 fee rows belong to tenant 2.
The 'staging' smartcity-os credential and the production one resolve to the same Neon endpoint and the same rows. Read the endpoint host before describing an app as pointed at non-production data.
DEAD-END: Trying to authorize the DO CLI with the MCP agent token to reach the Apps API for secret handling: it works for Apps/Droplets, but the CLI route is not needed — the constraint was never the tool, it was that a secret's plaintext must not appear in a command, a spec on disk that is not deleted, or a transcript.
Staging the clamp violation through the internal-context header path from the internet: refused twice, on both commits. Use a real session instead.

Adding the app's missing secrets as one spec update after creation: DO re-validates the whole spec and rejects any EV[...] it cannot decrypt, so the app either has its full environment from the start or the update fails wholesale.

Running the full vitest suite on this box as a gate: module import alone took minutes and produced four timing flakes that pass in isolation. Use it for signal, not as a verdict, and say which failures are environment.
